answers.query: How much urea and DAP do I need for two acres of maize?
answers.answer:
Your farm question
Fertilizer guide
Maize
Plan nutrients before buying another fertilizer

Use the crop stage, soil test and earlier applications together. A yellow leaf alone does not set a dose.

Steps you can take now
Write down the crop age, cultivated area, fertilizer names, amounts and dates already applied.
Use a recent soil test to identify missing nutrients rather than repeating the same product.
Use the fertilizer guide to convert an existing nutrient recommendation into product quantities.

To narrow it down: Which crop, age, area and fertilizers already applied? Do you have a soil report?

Why these steps? Sources
Conditional fertilizer quantity calculation

Detected area: 2 acres.

This is a high-input irrigated hybrid reference; rainfed maize may need much less. Nitrogen splits are 25% basal, 50% around day 25, and 25% around day 45. Full phosphorus and potash are basal in this reference.

Only if this saved reference fits your crop and growing conditions, the whole-season product equivalents are:

Calculated reference quantities, not a field-specific prescription
Product	kg / 2 acres
Urea (46% N)	388.24
DAP (18% N, 46% P₂O₅)	131.96
MOP (60% K₂O)	101.17

DAP nitrogen is deducted before calculating urea. These are season totals, not one application; already-applied nutrients and your soil recommendation must be accounted for. For maize, confirm irrigated hybrid versus rainfed/variety before using this reference.

Existing crop nutrient reference
Nutrient guidance for your crop

This is a high-input irrigated hybrid reference; rainfed maize may need much less. Nitrogen splits are 25% basal, 50% around day 25, and 25% around day 45. Full phosphorus and potash are basal in this reference.

A detected stage helps you discuss timing, but it does not establish a safe fertilizer dose. Use your soil report and record earlier applications.

TNAU Agritech — crop reference
